source.title: Overparameterized random feature regression with nearly orthogonal data

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material cutoff affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes random feature ridge regression with fixed random first-layer weights and ridge regression on the second layer. Its results concern concentration of regression errors around kernel regression and a generalization lower bound, not the claim versions about gradient-based training, classification error, shortcuts, initialization comparisons, learning-rate dynamics, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: No qualifying result rows: the training-error results are bounds on the difference between random feature ridge regression and kernel ridge regression, not reported training classification-error outcomes for the claim's gradient-training behavior. CIFAR-10 appears only as data used in a simulation comparing those two regression errors. Other relevant statements are theoretical results, not measurements of the behaviors named in the versions.
record.test_reason: The study fixes Gaussian first-layer weights and solves output-layer ridge regression analytically (Section 2.3). Its results concern regression-error approximation and generalization, not any version's gradient-training behavior. CIFAR-10 supplies inputs for synthetic teacher targets, not a classification-training test. Deep Information Propagation, an original source for V4, appears only as a background citation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under nearly orthogonal deterministic-data assumptions and sufficient width, RFRR approximates KRR; polynomial-kernel approximation then yields a generalization lower bound for higher-degree teacher components.
record.recipe_differences: Closed-form ridge regression trains only the second-layer weights while first-layer Gaussian weights remain fixed; the claim versions concern gradient-based training of networks and classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The theoretical bounds depend on dataset orthogonality, network width relative to sample size, activation function, ridge parameter, and—in the generalization analysis—the teacher and test-data assumptions. These dependencies do not test the settings named in the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated data and width assumptions, random feature ridge regression approaches kernel ridge regression in training error, cross-validation, and generalization error; Figures 1–3 illustrate shrinking differences with width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide fixed random-feature regression approximates its expected-kernel regression under nearly orthogonal data assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.13 lower-bounds generalization error by the teacher's Hermite-component energy above degree ℓ, up to a vanishing term.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nearly orthogonal data impose a polynomial approximation barrier on generalization by fixed random-feature regression.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2022)
record.problems: The empirical comparisons report differences between RFRR and KRR rather than absolute training classification error. The real-world CIFAR-10 simulation uses 800 selected features and 1000 normalized samples; the text says the nearly orthogonal condition is future work to verify for real-world datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows meet the required outcome and behavior criteria. Figure 1–3 show differences between RFRR and KRR training, cross-validation, and test errors; they do not report the gradient-training classification outcomes in the versions.

untested.parts: SGD/Adam training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization effects.
Gradient-descent convergence to spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons in ReLU teacher-student networks.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the result rows empty is appropriate for V1–V6. The polynomial generalization barrier does not establish optimization failure or spurious local minima. The record's AISTATS 2022 publication attribution is not established by the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No gradient-based training or training classification error is tested; labels are used in regression.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student gradient-descent experiment, spurious minima, or width comparison is tested.
No depth or shortcut comparison is tested.
No comparison of initializations for training speed or trainable depth is tested; Gaussian weights are fixed random features.
No learning-rate or training-stability experiment is tested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
